title: Wipro Cut 6,716 Jobs in September Quarter as Utilisation Slipped
excerpt: The Bengaluru IT major's workforce fell 2.8% to 236,328 in Q2 FY27, even as voluntary attrition eased to 13.8% and campus hiring plans stayed intact.
body:
• Wipro's headcount fell by 6,716 in the September quarter to 236,328, down 2.8% from 243,044 in the June quarter, though still 836 higher than a year earlier.
  • Voluntary attrition eased to 13.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, from 13.9% in Q1 and 14.9% a year ago, while net utilisation fell to 83.4% from 86.4% a year earlier.
  • Wipro gave no breakdown of why the workforce shrank; it onboarded roughly 1,000 fresh graduates in the first half of FY27 and reaffirmed a plan to hire about 7,500 campus recruits over the full year.
  • The jobs data sat alongside results already reported by The Videshi: revenue rose 9.1% year on year to Rs 24,752.7 crore while net profit fell 1.9% to Rs 3,200.6 crore.

Wipro reduced its workforce by 6,716 employees in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, taking its total headcount to 236,328 from 243,044 three months earlier, according to the company's quarterly datasheet reported by People Matters. The 2.8% sequential decline is the workforce detail that had not featured in earlier coverage of the quarter, and it reverses the expansion Wipro recorded through FY26, when its permanent workforce reached 242,156 at the end of March.

A Smaller Workforce, With No Explanation Attached

The published figures establish the scale of the reduction but not its causes. Wipro did not specify how much came from voluntary departures, restructuring or other changes, and attrition alone does not explain it: voluntary attrition actually improved during the quarter. Headcount also remains 836 above the year-ago level of 235,492, framing the move as a sharp quarterly contraction rather than a year-long downsizing.

Utilisation moved in the same direction as headcount. Net utilisation, excluding trainees, was 83.4% in Q2 FY27, down from 83.6% in the June quarter and three percentage points below the 86.4% recorded a year earlier. A company carrying fewer billable staff at lower utilisation is not simply trimming a bench; the figures point to softer deployment demand across the business during the quarter.

Attrition Eased Even as Numbers Fell

Voluntary attrition stood at 13.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, edging down from 13.9% in Q1 FY27 and well below the 14.9% of Q2 FY26, Indian Television reported. That combination — fewer employees leaving voluntarily, yet a much smaller total workforce — suggests the reduction was driven less by resignations than by slower intake and internal workforce decisions, although Wipro has not confirmed a breakdown.

"The strategic investments we have been making are beginning to deliver results."

— Srini Pallia, CEO and Managing Director, Wipro

Revenue Rose, Profit Did Not

The workforce cut came in a quarter of contrasting financials. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 9.1% year on year to Rs 24,752.7 crore, while consolidated net profit declined 1.9% to Rs 3,200.6 crore and fell 4.7% sequentially. IT services revenue was $2,611.5 million, flat in constant-currency terms sequentially, and the IT services operating margin improved to 16.5% from 16% in Q1. Operating cash flow rose 61.3% sequentially to about Rs 5,300 crore, equivalent to 165.8% of net income. The Videshi has already covered the earnings and the bookings slump in detail: total bookings fell 22.9% sequentially to $2.595 billion and large-deal bookings dropped 58.6% to $674 million, as reported in our earlier articles on Wipro's second-quarter revenue and its near four-year-low deal bookings.

Freshers Still Coming, AI Training at Scale

Entry-level hiring has not stopped. Wipro onboarded roughly 1,000 fresh graduates in the first half of the financial year and reaffirmed its intention to hire approximately 7,500 campus recruits across FY27. Its FY26 annual report counted 212,663 employees covered by AI-ready initiatives, 93,994 associates with a master AI certification, and 19.23 million learning hours. Those figures do not show how AI has changed demand for particular roles, but they show the bet: fewer general roles, more AI-credentialed staff.

What This Means for Tech Workers

For Indian technology workers, including the large diaspora workforce employed by Indian IT services firms in the United States and elsewhere, the practical reading is narrow and concrete: the fresher pipeline remains open at about 7,500 campus hires for the year, while experienced hiring faces a quarter in which the company let its total numbers fall by nearly 7,000 and ran utilisation three points below last year's level. Watch the December quarter's headcount and utilisation prints, not the attrition rate, for the first sign of a turn.

What Comes Next

Wipro has guided Q3 FY27 IT services revenue to between $2.571 billion and $2.625 billion, a constant-currency range of -1.5% to +0.5%. If bookings recover and headcount stabilises, the September workforce drop reads as a one-quarter adjustment. If utilisation falls again alongside another headcount decline, it becomes a trend that India's fourth-largest IT services exporter will have to explain directly.
